title: Embroidered greetings card
subtitle: A small motif worked on card-weight fabric, mounted in a ready-made card aperture
excerpt: An embroidered greetings card mounts a small stitched motif in a card aperture, making a handmade card that is also an embroidery project. The whole piece is completed in one sitting.
heroPrompt: Handmade embroidered greetings card, a small heart motif in red stem stitch visible through the card aperture, cream card, white background, flat lay.

content.text: An embroidered card is a contained project: a small motif (a heart, a flower, a set of initials) worked on a piece of fabric and then glued or taped inside a card aperture. Blank aperture cards with oval or square windows are sold in craft shops and online.

items.label: Fabric
items.value: White or cream cotton, 10 x 10 cm

items.label: Thread
items.value: 1 to 2 colours of stranded cotton, 2 strands

items.label: Card
items.value: Ready-made blank aperture card, aperture to suit your motif

content.text: Measure the card aperture and draw a motif that fits inside it with a small border. A 3 to 4 cm heart or flower works well in most standard apertures.
Transfer the motif to the centre of the fabric with a water-soluble pen. Mount in the hoop.
Embroider the motif. For a heart: work stem stitch around the outline with 2 strands. For a flower: stem stitch petals with French knot centres.
Remove from the hoop and damp the fabric to remove transfer marks. Press gently on the reverse while still damp.
Open the card flat. Centre the embroidered fabric behind the aperture. Fix with double-sided tape around the edge of the fabric, keeping tape clear of the embroidery.
Fold the card panel behind the aperture over the fabric to conceal the reverse. Press flat.
Keep the back layer of the card unglued so the recipient can open the card and read the inside in the normal way.
